headline: Certified proposed PY2024 Community Development Block Grant activities as consistent with city plans and ordinances.
summary: The Planning Director presented proposed Community Development Block Grant activities for El Centro, Macomber Stadium, Dexter Plaza, and Housing Authority exterior repairs. Members unanimously certified the activities as consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and local development ordinances and regulations. Approval of two sets of minutes was continued to the next regular meeting.
decisions: Certified the proposed Community Development Block Grant activities as consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and local ordinances and regulations, passed unanimously.
Continued approval of the August 26, 2026 and September 23, 2026 regular meeting minutes to the next regularly scheduled meeting, passed unanimously.

decision_titles: Proposed PY2024 Community Development Block Grant applications
Approval of August 26 and September 23, 2026 meeting minutes
plain_text:
CITY OF CENTRAL FALLS 
                 COMBINED PLANNING AND ZONING BOARD 
 
 
Page 1 of 3 
SPECIAL MEETING 
(PUBLIC HEARING) 
Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at 5:00 PM 
The Bessette Building (DPW) – 1280 High Street, Central Falls, RI 02863 
 
MINUTES 
I. Call to Order 
Chair Marenzana called the meeting to order at 5:02 PM 
II. Roll Call 
Chair Marenzana called the roll and the following members were present: John Marenzana, Hugo 
Figueroa, Ann Peckham, and Kevin Marchand. Also present were: James P. Vandermillen, Planning 
Director; Joshua B. Magnone, Planning Principal Deputy Director; and Joseph P. Baxter, Esq., Legal 
Counsel. 
III. Pledge of Allegiance 
Chair Marenzana led the Board in reciting the Pledge of Allegiance. 
IV. Approval of Minutes 
       A. Regular Meeting Minutes of August 26, 2026  
      B. Regular Meeting Minutes of September 23, 2026 
Mr. Magnone asked that approval of both minutes be continued to the next regularly scheduled 
meeting.  
Chair Marenzana entertained a motion to continue approval of the minutes to the next regularly 
scheduled meeting. Mr.  Marchand moved the motion, seconded by Mr. Figueroa. The vote was taken 
by a voice vote, all members voted in the affirmative. There was no objection, the motion passed 
unanimously. 
V. New Business 
A. Pursuant to its local and statutory authority as the Planning Board, discussion and possible vote on 
     proposed PY2024 Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Applications: 
     i. Presentation of proposed activities: 
     Mr. Vandermillen distributed a handout that summarizes all the City’s proposed CDBG activities. 
     Mr. Vandermillen clarified that these are proposed activities for CDBG Program Year 2025, except the 
     proposed activities for affordable housing which fall under CDBG Program Year 2024. 
     Mr. Vandermillen described why the City pursues these activities as well as the process for applying 
     for funds, including the Boards role in certifying compliance with local regulations prior to going to 
     the City Council for consideration. 
          1. Proposed Public Services Activities
Page 2 of 3 
     Mr. Vandermillen described how funding will be used to support services at El Centro, particularly 
                 by partnering with Elisha Project and Boys and Girls Club of Northern RI, including the services 
                 that these organizations will provide at the new community center. 
     Chair Marenzana asked Mr. Vandermillen to clarify which services Elisha Project are providing. Mr. 
                  Vandermillen responded by explaining that they will be operating the food market at El Centro. 
     Mr. Figueroa asked a question regarding another Elisha Project location on Roosevelt Ave. Mr. 
                 Marenzana and Mr. Vandermillen responded. 
          2. Proposed Public Facilities/Infrastructure Activities 
          Mr. Vandermillen described the proposal and need to improve the concessions, restrooms, and 
                 storage facilities at Macomber Stadium, an important community recreation site. 
    Mr. Vandermillen described the significance of Dexter Plaza to the community, how it has been 
                utilized, how the conditions are now inadequate, and how the goal of pursuing funding will be to 
                improve conditions on the site. 
    Mr. Figueroa asked a question regarding the use of State bonds at the Dexter Plaza site, in addition 
                to the City’s proposal to use CDBG funds. Mr. Vandermillen clarified that the money received from 
                the State are grants, the City does not have to pay them back, and the interest in apply for CDBG 
                funds is to cover the remainder of necessary project costs. 
          3. Proposed Affordable Housing Activities 
     Mr. Vandermillen described the activities that the City is pursuing on behalf of the Housing 
                 Authority to enable them to make exterior repairs to buildings. 
           Mr. Figueroa asked what work the Housing Authority performed last year on one of its buildings. 
           Mr. Vandermillen explained that they performed exterior work on one of their buildings that was 
                  in need of repair. 
           Mr. Figueroa asked if the Housing Authority’s properties are separate from the City.  
           Mr. Vandermillen replied by explaining that the Housing Authority, and its properties, are  
                  separate from the City, although the City works closely with them as a community partner. 
    ii. Review of proposed activities to determine compliance with City’s Comprehensive Plan and 
               Development Ordinances and Regulations 
        Mr. Vandermillen provided a handout to the Board which describes how each of the proposed 
               activities are consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and local development ordinances and 
               regulations. 
        Mr. Vandermillen read the handout aloud to the Board. 
        Mr. Vandermillen also provided a separate handout covering how the proposed stormwater 
               management projects at Dexter Plaza are consistent with the Comprehensive Plan. 
        Ms. Peckham asked about how improved restroom facilities will be secured when not in use at 
               Macomber Stadium. Mr. Vandemillen responded by stating that facilities will be closed when not 
               being utilized for events. 
   Mr. Vandermillen asked the Board if they had any questions regarding his descriptions of the 
               activites. 
   iii. Discussion and possible vote with respect to certification of compliance with City’s 
               Comprehensive Plan and Development Ordinances and Regulations
Page 3 of 3 
  Chair Marenzana entertained a motion to certify that the proposed activities, as presented, are 
         consistent with local development policies set forth in the Comprehensive Plan and with local 
         development ordinances and regulations. Mr.  Marchand moved the motion, seconded by Ms. 
         Peckham. The vote was taken by a voice vote, all members voted in the affirmative. There was no 
         objection, the motion passed unanimously. 
VI. Adjournment 
Chair Marenzana entertained a motion to adjourn the meeting. Mr.  Marchand moved the motion, 
seconded by Mr. Figueroa. The vote was taken by a voice vote, all members voted in the affirmative. 
There was no objection, the motion passed unanimously. The meeting stood adjourned at 5:39 PM.
